subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should OpenClaw grant device-less shared-token WebSocket clients configured operator scopes, trust client-requested scopes after token auth, or keep requiring device identity for scoped remote operator RPCs?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug affects real remote/multi-agent workflows, but the direct fix changes who may hold operator scopes on network-reachable Gateway connections.

options.title: Bound configured token scopes
options.body: Land a reviewed token-scope or device-token policy that keeps default clearing but lets trusted deployments opt into specific scopes with exposure guards and tests.

options.title: Trust requested scopes after token auth
options.body: Directly preserve client-declared scopes for successful shared-token auth, which fixes the symptom but broadens the shared-token trust boundary.

options.title: Keep device identity required
options.body: Document current scope clearing as the supported security boundary and close the bug only after offering a clear migration path for affected deployments.

recommendation.title: Bound configured token scopes
recommendation.body: Land a reviewed token-scope or device-token policy that keeps default clearing but lets trusted deployments opt into specific scopes with exposure guards and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current open token-scope implementation path and has recent history in the shared-auth baseline.
